reason: This text fragment from Exodus 2:16-22 narrates Moses' encounter with the daughters of Reuel (the Midianite priest) at a well, his assistance in helping them water their flock, and his subsequent marriage to Zipporah. The passage contains no depiction of Hebrew ingratitude toward leaders or Yahweh. Rather, it presents Moses (a Hebrew leader in exile) performing a virtuous action by helping the women against the shepherds. The narrative focuses on personal events and relationships, not on expressions of ingratitude or dissatisfaction from the Hebrew people.
